title: Lifts of exact functors to module objects are exact
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be abelian monoidal categories whose tensor products are additive in
each variable. Let $\mathcal R$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal S$ a monoid object of
$\mathcal D$ such that $\mathcal R\otimes-$ and $\mathcal S\otimes-$ are right exact, so that
$\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ and $\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal D)$ are abelian
([lem-sfb-modobj-abelian]); write $U_{\mathcal R}$, $U_{\mathcal S}$ for the forgetful functors. Let
$F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an additive exact functor and
$G\colon\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal D)$ a functor with
$U_{\mathcal S}\circ G=F\circ U_{\mathcal R}$. Then $G$ is additive and exact; in particular it preserves
finite limits and finite colimits.

proof.text: By [def-galois-exact-functor], right exactness of $T_{\mathcal R}=\mathcal R\otimes-$ and $T_{\mathcal S}=\mathcal S\otimes-$ means preservation of finite colimits. Thus [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies to both monoids: both module categories are abelian. Use the composition convention $ba=b\circ a$. The module-morphism equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is $a\gamma_M=\gamma_N T(a)$. Its solutions are closed under addition, zero and negatives, by bilinearity of composition and additivity of $T$: for instance $(a+b)\gamma_M=\gamma_N(Ta+Tb)=\gamma_NT(a+b)$. Hence the Hom groups and the additive forgetful functors are inherited from the base categories. For parallel module maps $a,b$, the assumed commutation gives $U_{\mathcal S}G(a+b)=F(U_{\mathcal R}a+U_{\mathcal R}b)=U_{\mathcal S}Ga+U_{\mathcal S}Gb=U_{\mathcal S}(Ga+Gb)$. Faithfulness [lem-sfb-modobj-forget-faithful] gives $G(a+b)=Ga+Gb$, which is additivity [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]; setting $a=b=0$ and subtracting also gives $G(0)=0$.

source.place: Additivity paragraph, with the abelian-category hypotheses checked first

proof.text: The source forgetful functor $U_{\mathcal R}$ preserves all kernels and cokernels. Indeed, for a module morphism $\varphi$, choose an underlying kernel $k_0:K_0\to U_{\mathcal R}M$. The statement of [lem-sfb-modobj-kernels] equips $K_0$ with an action and makes $k_0$ a module kernel. For any other module kernel $k:K\to M$, the two universal properties give module maps $v:K\to K_0$ and $w:K_0\to K$ with $k_0v=k$, $kw=k_0$; uniqueness gives $wv=1$ and $vw=1$. Their underlying maps are inverse, so $U_{\mathcal R}k=(U_{\mathcal R}k_0)(U_{\mathcal R}v)$ is an underlying kernel. For cokernels, [lem-sfb-modobj-cokernels] supplies an action on a chosen underlying cokernel $q_0:U_{\mathcal R}N\to Q_0$, making $q_0$ a module cokernel; its finite-colimit hypothesis holds by step 1. Comparing any module cokernel $q:N\to Q$ with $q_0$ gives inverse module maps $v:Q_0\to Q$, $w:Q\to Q_0$ satisfying $vq_0=q$, $wq=q_0$. Thus $U_{\mathcal R}q=(U_{\mathcal R}v)(U_{\mathcal R}q_0)$ is an underlying cokernel. These comparisons use only the kernel property (unique factorization of maps killed by $\varphi$), respectively the dual cokernel property.

source.place: Exactness paragraph, first and fourth sentences: spell out comparison with the constructed (co)kernels

proof.text: The target forgetful functor reflects kernels. Suppose $\varphi:M\to N$ and $k:K\to M$ are module maps with $\varphi k=0$ and underlying $k$ a kernel. Given a module map $\psi:P\to M$ with $\varphi\psi=0$, let $u:UP\to UK$ be its unique underlying factorization, $ku=\psi$. Using the module-morphism equations of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], compute $ku\gamma_P=\psi\gamma_P=\gamma_M T_{\mathcal S}\psi=\gamma_M T_{\mathcal S}k\,T_{\mathcal S}u=k\gamma_K T_{\mathcal S}u$. A kernel arrow is monic: two maps with equal composites with it are factorizations of the same map through that kernel, so are equal by uniqueness. Cancelling $k$ therefore gives $u\gamma_P=\gamma_K T_{\mathcal S}u$, making $u$ a module map. Uniqueness is the underlying uniqueness, since module morphisms are underlying morphisms satisfying an equation. This is the module kernel universal property.

The target forgetful functor reflects cokernels. Suppose $q:N\to Q$ is a module map with $q\varphi=0$ and underlying $q$ a cokernel of $U\varphi$. For any module map $\psi:N\to P$ killed by $\varphi$, the underlying property supplies a unique $u:UQ\to UP$ with $uq=\psi$. Put $T=T_{\mathcal S}$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], $u\gamma_Q Tq=uq\gamma_N=\psi\gamma_N=\gamma_P T\psi=\gamma_P Tu\,Tq$. Right exactness in [def-galois-exact-functor] preserves this finite coequalizer of $U\varphi$ and $0$; additivity gives $T0=0$, so $Tq$ is a cokernel of $T(U\varphi)$. A cokernel arrow $e$ is epic directly from uniqueness: if $ae=be$, both $a,b$ factor the same map through $e$, so $a=b$. Cancel $Tq$ to obtain $u\gamma_Q=\gamma_P Tu$. Thus $u$ is a module map, and its uniqueness is underlying uniqueness. This proves the module cokernel universal property without an uncited assertion about preservation of arbitrary epimorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph U_S reflects cokernels, replacing the general epimorphism claim by preservation of this cokernel

proof.text: Let $k$ be any module kernel of $\varphi$ in the source category. Step 2 makes $U_{\mathcal R}k$ an underlying kernel. A kernel is the equalizer of $U_{\mathcal R}\varphi$ and $0$, a finite diagram. Exactness of $F$ in [def-galois-exact-functor] therefore makes $F(U_{\mathcal R}k)$ a kernel of $F(U_{\mathcal R}\varphi)$, since additivity makes $F(0)=0$. The assumed equality of composite functors identifies these maps with $U_{\mathcal S}Gk$ and $U_{\mathcal S}G\varphi$. Also $G\varphi\,Gk=G(0)=0$ by step 1, so step 3 proves $Gk$ is a module kernel. For a source module cokernel $q$, step 2 and finite-colimit preservation by $F$ make $U_{\mathcal S}Gq=F(U_{\mathcal R}q)$ an underlying cokernel of $U_{\mathcal S}G\varphi$ (the coequalizer of that map and zero). Step 4 and $Gq\,G\varphi=0$ then show $Gq$ is a module cokernel. Consequently $G$ preserves every kernel and every cokernel.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-kernel-cokernel-finite-exactness] to $G$ between the abelian module categories from step 1. Its additivity is step 1 and its preservation of all kernels and cokernels is step 5, so both clauses apply: $G$ preserves finite limits and finite colimits. By [def-galois-exact-functor], this is exactly exactness. The additivity already proved gives every clause of the assertion.
